_note: Run these against an offline sandbox that compiles the model like Cube, or against a sandbox org. A wrong column path or stream breaks the whole org's semantic model, so never run them against production. Fixture: the cubes crm_companies, crm_deals (count and total_amount measures), and crm_contacts; deals and contacts join many_to_one to companies. Table Companies is rooted on crm_companies with columns id (hidden), name, industry, country, and crm_deals_count (a measure); country is a scoring feature. Table Deals is rooted on crm_deals with columns id (hidden), name, stage, amount, and next_step (stored). Segment 'Stalled deals' is DYNAMIC and READY, rooted on crm_deals.

evals.prompt: Make a table of our contacts with their email, first and last name.
evals.expected_output: Creates a table with the name only, then one update with the root stream crm_contacts (no joinPath). Columns: an external id on the primary key, plus email, first_name, and last_name, all read from crm_contacts. Verifies with meta and a view query.
expectations: Exactly one new table exists, created with a name-only body
Its only stream is { id: crm_contacts }, with no joinPath, connectionId or streamName
It has an external id column on crm_contacts.id
It has external email, first_name and last_name columns reading crm_contacts
The org's model compiles at the end
Called meta or queried the new table's view after the last write

evals.prompt: Create a table of the stalled deals.
evals.expected_output: Finds the existing 'Stalled deals' segment, creates a table rooted on crm_deals with id (hidden) and name columns, and sets the default view's segmentId to that segment. Doesn't create a new segment or filter.
expectations: Exactly one new table exists, rooted on crm_deals with an external id column
The new table's default view has segmentId = the Stalled deals segment
No ad-hoc filter on the new table's views
The org's model compiles at the end

evals.prompt: Add the company's industry to the Deals table.
evals.expected_output: Reads the Deals table and keeps all 5 columns with their ids. Adds a stream { id: crm_companies, joinPath: crm_deals.crm_companies } with no connectionId or streamName, and an external industry column reading crm_companies.industry. The root stays crm_deals.
expectations: All 5 original Deals columns are still there with their original ids
Deals has a new external column with streamId crm_companies and path industry
crm_companies is a stream of Deals with joinPath crm_deals.crm_companies, and crm_deals is still the first stream
No stream in the update body carries connectionId or streamName
The org's model compiles at the end
Called meta or queried the Deals view after the last write

evals.prompt: Add the deal stage to the Companies table.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that a company has many deals, so a deal-stage dimension column would repeat rows. Doesn't add a non-measure column reading crm_deals, explains why, and offers alternatives: a measure such as a count per stage, or the Deals table.
expectations: Companies has no non-measure external column reading crm_deals at the end
All 5 original Companies columns are still there with their original ids
The org's model compiles at the end
Reply explains that a company has many deals (one-to-many or fan-out)

evals.prompt: Remove the country column from the Companies table.
evals.expected_output: Reads the table and sees that country feeds the score (scoringFeatures has columnId col4). Doesn't remove it, explains why, and points the user to the RevOS UI's column delete.
expectations: The country column (id col4) is still on Companies at the end, and the agent didn't try to remove it
The org's model compiles at the end
Reply says the column is used for scoring
Reply points the user to the RevOS UI

evals.expected_output: Reads the Deals table, describes it (rows are deals, 5 columns, next_step is stored), checks segments and tables for anything reading model_<Deals id> or its own cube, says the delete is permanent and takes the stored next_step values with it, and asks for an explicit yes. Doesn't call api_delete in this turn.
expectations: Deals still exists at the end of the turn
No api_delete call was made
Before replying, listed the org's segments and tables (and the stored cubes) to check what reads the Deals view or its own cube
Reply says the delete can't be undone and names what goes with it (stored values such as next_step)
Reply asks the user to confirm deleting this table
